quarantine.abstract_text: In the drug discovery field, drug affinity has long been considered the gold standard for designing small compounds with therapeutic activity. However, since the beginning of the 21st century, kinetic parameters, which are directly related to compound efficacy, have increasingly been recognized as central to the rational design of new drugs. However, such data are scarce, while the experimental determination of the association and dissociation rate constants, k on and k off, is costly and time-consuming. Molecular simulations, such as Molecular Dynamics (MD) calculations have been proposed to predict those kinetic constants, despite known limitations. With the rapid development of AI-based tools, researchers are now proposing advanced methodologies that leverage both data-driven learning from existing datasets and physics-based modelling through MD simulations. This review presents a critical overview of MD-based approaches for estimating protein-ligand binding free energies and rate constants. It then examines data-driven prediction methods and ML-assisted molecular simulations, with particular attention to validation and current limitations. Finally, it discusses the crucial need for new data with respect to the FAIR principles and methodological developments needed to further improve prediction quality.

quarantine.venue: Journal of Inclusive Methodology and Technology in Learning and Teaching

quarantine.abstract_text: Writing a Social Story requires information about the learner and the situation, together with attention to language and accuracy. Generative artificial intelligence may assist with drafting, but its output requires review before educational use. This paper describes a Social Stories™ generation tool developed within the Socrate platform at the University of Salerno as part of a project supporting Individualized Education Plan design. The tool combines a module for collecting educational information with a technical module for configuring generation and review. Users specify the learner’s communication profile, the context, the story’s purpose and available support. A Python backend coordinates language model generation, automated checks and revision, with separate drafting and reviewing roles. The procedures are designed to identify structural problems, unsupported assumptions and coercive or judgmental wording. Teachers retain responsibility for checking the narrative and deciding whether it is appropriate for the learner. Feedback and revision records provide material for professional discussion and training. The paper outlines the tool’s architecture and the evaluation needed to assess narrative quality and educational use. Future work will compare local and general-purpose models through expert assessment and examine whether stories support learners’ understanding in the situations for which they are written.

quarantine.abstract_text: The engagement of students with Special Educational Needs (SEN) depends on instructional design that reduces barriers without lowering cognitive challenge, yet personalisation is often hard to sustain in everyday teaching. This paper reports a pilot study in a vocational upper secondary school, where a Large Language Model-based mediation device, combining a «low-impact» micro-design template, a SEN Matrix anchored to ICF descriptors and an engineered prompt, supported co-design between the subject teacher and the special education teacher. Through an exploratory multiple case study, we examine the match between recorded barriers and generated mediators and the experience reported by two students with individualised plans following an equivalent curriculum after a lesson designed with the device. The mediators addressed the instructional barriers in the Matrix, but not the relational or home-study ones; the students reported benefits, no distraction and the sense that the lesson had been designed for them. We discuss the researchers’ role in producing the materials, the study’s limitations and the prospect of agents that support the design dialogue between teachers.
